headline: Patched Apple flaw exploited to spread info-stealers; WordPress KEV patch due Nov 6; $6.3B Binance heist leads coverage

bullets.text: New: The Hacker News reports hackers are exploiting a patched Apple flaw to deliver info-stealing malware, citing CISA. CISA KEV lists CVE-2024-27834, added 2026-11-04, with a federal due date of 2026-11-18.
Developing, Binance, 8 outlets and the biggest story on the board: TechCrunch reports researchers warned of North Korean hacking tactics years before the record $6.3B heist.

Still active, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.
Still active, critical: BleepingComputer reports Zyxel has fixed a zero-day that was exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches.
Still active, high: The Hacker News reports a critical Rails flaw lets attackers write server files through crafted ImageMagick uploads. Dark Reading also warns that vulnerable servers are at risk.
Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: SecurityWeek reports malicious updates served in an OpsShield supply chain attack. BleepingComputer says the hijacked autoupdate deployed a backdoor and stole data.

actions: Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 (KEV due 2026-11-06).
Patch Apple devices for CVE-2024-27834 (KEV due 2026-11-18) and keep iOS and Android current against the APT29-linked n-day exploits.
Check Rails advisories and patch apps that accept ImageMagick uploads. Apply Debian and Ubuntu APT fixes as they become available.
Apply Zyxel's switch zero-day fix and patch Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527; check both for compromise.
DreamHost: change FTP passwords, end webmail sessions. mSecure: follow its password reset warnings. cPGuard: hunt the backdoor.
Check whether your firm works with Lab 1 and, if so, review what data it held and any notice it sent.
